chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not create anything except that He created for it a cause/reason.'
He said: 'And He did not create anything except that He created for it a cause/reason, except for Faith (Iman).'
He said: 'And He did not create anything except that He created for it a cause/reason, except for Faith, for verily Allah, the Exalted, created Faith without a cause/reason.'

He said: 'And He did not create anything except that He created for it a cause/reason, except for Faith, for verily Allah, the Exalted, created Faith without a cause/reason, and He created Faith for His own sake.'
ai.seo_question: Why is Faith considered unique among all created things in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this distinction to affirm the direct divine bestowal of Faith, distinguishing it from the contingent nature of the physical world. This underscores the Shia theological emphasis on *Tawhid* in creation, where Iman is not merely a human acquisition but a sacred trust (*amanah*) originating directly from Allah's will.
